 Order

This miscellaneous appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 being aggrieved of award dated 30.09.2022 passed by 25th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur in MACC No.3901/2019, for enhancement of compensation.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that on 22/06/2019 at about 08:30 P.M., when appellant along with his friend was going by walking to Jarjola Hanuman Temple and as they reached in front of Lodhi Samajal Samudaik Bhavan, at the same time, the Respondent No.1 by driving motorcycle bearing No. MP-49-MP-0709 coming from back side dashed the appellant, due to which, he was grievously injured and received number of injuries on his body parts, immediately after accident he was taken to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9706 2 MA-602-2023 Hospital.

The information regarding accident has been given to police station Kotwali, Distt. Narshingpur and the same has been registered with Crime No. 443/19 against the respondent no.1.
3.

It is further submitted that learned Claims Tribunal has only considered 25% permanent disability, whereas as per disability certificate Ex. P-20 he sustained 80% permanent disability and at the time of accident he was working as Clothes Hawking and after the accident he is unable to earn his livelihood, therefore, amount need to be enhanced.

Learned Claims Tribunal applied multiplier of 16 as per Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation judgment finding as given at Sachin Nema vs Pradeep Patel on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162005315/
1 para 27 of the award amount which is not correct and multiplier of 18 will be applied.

sentences.text: Claims Tribunal has only awarded Rs.20,000/- on the head of special died.

Learned Claims Tribunal did not award any amount for lifetime helper to the appellant because due to this accident, he is unable to perform his daily works as well as without help he did not move and walk.

In these circumstances,
he made a prayer to enhance Rs.10,00,000/- in awarded amount i.e. Rs.8,20,900/-.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondents opposed the prayer and supported the passed by Claims Tribunal.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

On perusal of record, it is found that the age of appellant/claimant is 21 years and as per the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 SC, the multiplier of 18 ought to have been considered, but Claims Tribunal has applied only multiplier of 16.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, after considering multiplication of 18 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9706 3 MA-602-2023 on the head of loss of income due to permanent disability.
As the incident had occurred on 22.06.2019, therefore, Claims Tribunal ought to have considered Rs.6,500/- per month income of the claimant in place of Rs.6,000/- per month.

It is also found that the Claims Tribunal has considered only 25% permanent disability of appellant whereas, the medical board has issued a handicap certificate (Ex.P-20) regarding 80%
permanent disability of appellant/claimant.
Claims Tribunal has also mention any specific reason that on what basis he assumed 25% permanent disability of appellant/claimant.
7. Learned Claims Tribunal did not awarded any amount for future treatment which also needs to be enhanced because as per doctor advise he needs regular treatment.
Tribunal only awarded Rs.20,000/- for special diet and nutrition and Rs.20,000/- for physical and mental pain, which is too low, therefore, it also needs to be enhanced.

8. Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and after evaluating the record, this Court is of the view that the learned Claims Tribunal by assuming 25% permanent disability in place of 80% of appellant/claimant has awarded only Rs.8,20,900/- which is not sufficient.
9.

In view of aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference to enhance the lump sum amount of compensation i.e.
Rs.4,00,000/-, the said amount shall carry the same interest as has been awarded by the learned Tribunal.
The rest of conditions imposed by the learned Tribunal be as it is.
It is made clear that the appellant is entitled for getting interest on the aforesaid amount from the date of filing of this appeal i.e. 27/01/2023.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9706 4 MA-602-2023 10.
Accordingly, present appeal is a l l o w e d enhancing the compensation to the tune of Rs.4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh only) subject to following conditions:-
